reason: The replacement support needs a broad footing, so the excavator can prepare the ground first.
expectation: The excavator will prepare a stable footing for the replacement support.

effect: The excavator exposed firm ground beside the cribbing; the footing still needs to be built.
reaction: The distinction between clearing ground and making the footing is reassuring.
reason: Steel is the available structural material, and the prepared ground is the natural place to make the broad footing.
expectation: The steel will form a footing or base for the replacement support.

effect: The steel and prepared ground produced a braced replacement leg; it now needs to support the lander.
reaction: The broad plates and block footing make the load path clear.
reason: The replacement leg matches the lander's sound joints, so it should be fitted to the tilted lander.
expectation: The leg will be installed to restore a level launch platform.

effect: The replacement support is installed and carries the lander's weight; the launch platform is level and the chapter is complete.
reaction: The ladder reaching the ground straight is a satisfying callback to the awkward landing.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the replacement leg was most worthwhile: the plates, blocks and braced frame made the load path understandable.

leastWorthwhile.text: Clearing the ground was straightforward preparation, though it established a sensible foundation for the repair.

surprise.text: I expected the steel to make only a footing, but it produced the complete replacement leg on the prepared ground.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; each followed from preparing, building and installing the support.

continue.text: Yes. The practical repair was satisfying, and I would be curious to see how the return unfolds.
